text:
Alex C.: Quick proposal — SLO Policy Operator API to drive routing + model-variant fallbacks per customer tier/region. Want API shape + console UX feedback. TL;DR: declare p95 latency ms, availability %, circuit-breaker thresholds, fallback variants, and a degradation budget.

Priya M.: Nice. How do we interpret p95 across mixed hosts/regions? per-route or global? :thinking:

Alex C.: Per-route + per-region buckets. We store histograms keyed by (customer_id, route, region). The operator evaluates buckets over a sliding window and flips routing decisions.

Jamie L.: API sketch would help. Something like: 
```
{
  "policy_id": "gold-fast-fallback",
  "selector": {"customer_tier": "gold", "route": "generate/text"},
  "targets": {"p95_latency_ms": 150, "availability_pct": 99.5},
  "circuit_breaker": {"error_rate_pct": 2, "consecutive_minutes": 5},
  "fallbacks": [
    {"model": "redwood-lite-quant", "max_degradation_pct": 10},
    {"model": "open-small-v2", "max_degradation_pct": 30}
  ],
  "rollout": {"canary_pct": 10, "auto_revert_on_violation": true}
}
```

Daniela R.: Love the shape. Two concerns: 1) telemetry tags need to include fallback_model and policy_id so we can trace regressions; 2) need contract checks for model outputs so fallback doesn't break callers.

Priya M.: Also need clear console affordance: show active policy, current SLO windows, and a "why" trace when fallback is used. Maybe a timeline graph and a per-candidate cost delta.

Jamie L.: On the operator side, do we push policy to routers or have central decision service? I'd prefer centralized decision with cached routes in proxies for latency. Fallback decision is quick: check current health + degradation budget.

Alex C.: Agreed on central, with short TTL pins in edge proxies. Proxies pick up pin via config watch. If central is down, proxies use last-good policy and degrade to safe fallback model.

infra-bot: policy-validator: schema check passed for policy "gold-fast-fallback". deploy-check: capacity available in eu-west-1 for fallback pool.

Daniela R.: Quotas interplay: if fallback is cheaper but hits committed capacity, we must enforce per-customer reserved pools. Otherwise customers will see silent throttles. Also, what about retries — we should avoid routing loops.

Alex C.: Good call. We'll add fields: reserved_capacity, retry_policy (max_attempts, backoff), and a loop-detection header.

Priya M.: For rollouts UX: allow staged enablement by customer segments, and a preview mode where console simulates decisions using recent telemetry without applying them. Helps safety.

Jamie L.: Testing matrix: unit tests for decision logic, e2e with canary customers, chaos test where models go OOM, and performance test for central decision < 1ms median.

Daniela R.: One more thing: fallback contract checks need a lightweight schema validator and a similarity score threshold for embeddings/generation when exact format matters. Add a "contract_check" block in policy.

Alex C.: Good. I'll draft an RFC with the API, console mockups, and migration notes (default policy for existing customers = "pass-through") and list of telemetry tags. Planning to sync this Thursday 10am. @Priya M. @Jamie L. can you review before then? :thumbsup:

Priya M.: Yep, will review.

Jamie L.: I'll add perf SLIs and a small prototype for the decision cache.

infra-bot: scheduled meeting created: #eng-platform Thursday 10:00.

Alex C.: Thanks — will post RFC link shortly.
